analysis.title: SiteOne Landscape Supply Inc. (SITE): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: SITE reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $138.3mn vs GS estimate $137.1mn and FactSet consensus $133.1mn. The roughly 1% beat vs GS came mainly from higher other operating income (+2% to EBITDA) and an adjusted EBIT margin of 7.5%, 25bps above GS forecast (+1%).
3Q26 revenue rose 3% (organic -1%, M&A +3%) vs GS estimate of +4% (organic +1%, M&A +3%), a -1% shortfall.

Adj. EBITDA margin expanded 60bps YoY, which GS attributes to progress on commercial and operational initiatives. This came despite soft underlying market demand and delayed fall applications, which hurt volumes and caused about 20bps of SG&A margin deleverage in 3Q.
Management plans to cut headcount further and consolidate branches in 4Q, with an expected $6-8mn headwind to adj. EBITDA.

The 2026 adj. EBITDA guide was cut 2% to $433mn at the midpoint, vs GS estimate $437mn and consensus $431mn. GS reads this as baseline operating expectations largely unchanged excluding the restructuring action.
Net debt/EBITDA was 1.2x at 3Q end, vs 1.3x last quarter and 1.0x in 3Q25, with $88mn of cash. 3Q FCF was $108mn vs GS forecast $126mn.
SITE repurchased $62mn of shares in 3Q and completed one acquisition. The Board approved a $500mn increase in the buyback, leaving about $538mn available including about $38mn on the prior plan.
GS rates SITE Neutral with a $100 12-month price target, based on 10.5x its Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA forecast. The stock closed at $103.03 on 27 Oct 2026, 2.9% above the target.

GS call topics: fall demand in residential and non-residential, digital and private label initiatives, competition and pricing under inflation, SG&A savings from the workforce reduction, fuel costs and gross margin, and integration of recent acquisitions.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and a $100 target (10.5x Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA) after a slight 3Q EBITDA beat and a 2026 guide cut tied to restructuring. The stock trades 2.9% above the target.

sector_views.rationale: GS cites persistent softness in underlying market demand and delayed fall applications. Upside risks are a recovery in discretionary repair & remodel, and downside risks are a failed housing starts recovery and weak commercial construction.

earnings_insights: SITE 3Q26 reported adj. EBITDA $138.3mn vs GS est $137.1mn and FactSet consensus est $133.1mn (reported 10/28/2026).
3Q26 revenue +3% reported (organic -1%, M&A +3%) vs GS est +4% (organic +1%, M&A +3%). Adj. EBIT margin 7.5% reported, 25bps above GS est.
FY2026 adj. EBITDA guidance cut 2% to $433mn at the midpoint, vs GS est $437mn and consensus est $431mn. 4Q restructuring expected to cost $6-8mn of adj. EBITDA.
3Q26 FCF reported $108mn vs GS est $126mn. Net debt/EBITDA 1.2x. Share repurchases of $62mn in 3Q.
GS estimates: FY26E revenue $4,911.0mn, EBITDA $409.6mn, EPS $3.95. FY27E revenue $5,074.5mn, EBITDA $446.6mn, EPS $4.99. FY28E EPS $6.24.
GS quarterly EPS estimates: 9/26E $1.48, 12/26E $(0.19), 3/27E $(0.42). 6/26 EPS was $3.17.
risk_factors: Upside risks to Neutral: recovery in discretionary repair & remodel, inflationary pressures benefiting results, accretive M&A, and success of company-specific initiatives.
Downside risks: housing starts recovery fails to materialize, weaker commercial construction, greater competition if peers seek share, and adverse weather exacerbating seasonality.
Near-term pressures: persistent soft demand, delayed fall applications, SG&A deleverage, and higher fuel costs.
